hook: The sculptor of David and painter of the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

pages.x: Michelangelo Buonarroti was born in 1475 at Caprese, near Florence, and was nursed by a stonecutter's wife. He joked that he had drunk in his love of the chisel with her milk. At 13 he joined a painter's workshop, and soon Lorenzo de' Medici took him into his own household.

In the Medici sculpture garden he mocked the work of another student, Pietro Torrigiano, who punched him so hard that he broke his nose. It stayed flattened for the rest of his life, as you can see in his portraits.

At 23 he carved the Pietà for St Peter's in Rome: Mary holding the dead Jesus across her lap. Hearing visitors credit it to another sculptor, he crept in at night and carved his name across Mary's sash. It is the only work he ever signed.

Back in Florence he carved a David over five metres tall from a block of marble that other sculptors had given up on. Finished in 1504, it shows the shepherd boy calm and ready before fighting Goliath, and became the symbol of the city.

From 1508 to 1512 Pope Julius II had him paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, though he protested he was a sculptor. Standing on scaffolding, head bent back, paint dripping on his face, he covered it with more than 300 figures, among them God reaching out to give life to Adam.

In his sixties he painted The Last Judgement on the chapel's altar wall. A papal official complained about all the naked bodies, so Michelangelo painted him into Hell, with donkey ears and a snake biting him.
At 71 he became chief architect of St Peter's Basilica, refusing any pay, and designed its huge dome, finished after his death. He died in 1564, nearly 89, still working.
Michelangelo was the greatest sculptor of the Renaissance, a supreme painter and a great architect. People called him "the divine one" in his own lifetime.
